coordinates.note: The only coordinate source found (checked 2026-09-17) is an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim geocoder lookup, which gives a campus-grade point. Read it as the general CERN-site area this marker names, not a surveyed detector-cavern position; it is shown as approximate. A survey or an official CERN coordinate for the cavern would give a better point. For this reason the ALEPH detector has no placement of its own at this site: the link is stated in the text and through the collaboration's host site.

name: LEP Point 4 (ALEPH)
notes: The point number is directly sourced ('Located at point 4 of the LEP ring', CERN Courier ALEPH page). The coordinates are an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for the surface marker 'CERN - Point 4', by the same method used for the ATLAS Point 1 record. No official CERN or geodetic publication consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives surveyed coordinates for this cavern.

summary.plain: The underground cavern at Point 4 of the LEP ring, near the French village of Echenevex, where the ALEPH detector recorded electron-positron collisions from 1989 to 2000.
summary.technical: LEP interaction point 4, in the commune of Echenevex (Ain, France); housed the ALEPH detector for the full LEP programme. The same tunnel point today carries only accelerating RF equipment for the LHC, not a detector.
